label: input token e at original positions 2-6
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is the letter e during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions t=2..6, and every such step fires. It never fires on e at t=0, 1, 7 or 8, on any other token, or at the delimiter or in the copy phase (including when e is fed back as output). Position shapes the magnitude: e at t=3-4 gives the strongest activations (near max, about 1.75) and carries roughly two thirds of the activation mass. e at t=2 is weak (about 0.15-0.3 of max) and e at t=6 is also weak. Dev split: precision, recall and F1 are all 1.0.

issues: No substantive issues. On the test split the predicate scores precision 0.99998, recall 1.0, F1 0.99999 and mass recall 1.0. Coverage is 1.0 in every activation quartile. There are 0 missed activations and 1 false positive: an e at t=6, L=7, which is isolated noise.

The dev profile backs up the factual claims. All activation is in the original phase (delimiter and copy phase are 0). The only token that fires is e (33% of e steps, which matches e at t=2..6 out of all e steps). Activation is 0 at t=0, 1 and 7+. Within orig_idx 2..6 the firing rate is a flat 0.033, so every e at those positions fires.

The magnitude claims hold. t=3 and t=4 carry 0.331 + 0.327 = 0.658 of the activation mass (about two thirds). From mass share divided by count, the mean activation at t=2 is about 0.27 of the t=3 mean, and at t=6 about 0.4 of the t=5 mean, so both ends are weak, as claimed.
The label 'input token e at original positions 2-6' matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
